Unit 2 Aim is, thus, a yardstick by which we can measure the success and failure of work done in school. Clear determination of educational aim can only ensure development of life in the right direction, towards reaching the goal. Behind any scientific plan and programme, there is a clear cut aim and purpose. Aims are necessary for efficient school management also. It helps in proper planning of the curriculum, library, method of teaching, selection of teachers, selection of teaching aids and apparatus, system of evaluation, standard of discipline etc. which dependens on the aims of education. From the point of view of teachers and guardians also, aims are necessary, because the society reviews and appreciates the work of the school in terms of its aims. In a democratic society, this assumes much greater importance. Finally, aims provide continuity and significance to education. We know that education is a continuous and dynamic process. It is a process of living through a continuous reconstruction of experiences, i.e., unfolding new dimension of knowledge, developing new capacities in the individual which is not possible without having aim of education. Unit 2 Aims of Education development of certain aims. Different educationists have put forward their views regarding aims of education. But then, there is no single aim of education which is acceptable to all. Moreover, aims are not static. They go on changing from time to time and from country to country, depending on the philosophy of life, political ideologies and socio-economic condition of a country. Broadly speaking, there have emerged two important aims of education, one emphasizing the development of individuality and the other giving stress on social development, i.e., social and civic efficiency. The root of these two aims may be attributed to two basic philosophical ideals of individualism and collectivism. Some other specific aims are formulated on the basis of intrinsic values and universal elements. key_points: 3 CONCEPT AND MEANING OF CURRICULUM We are all familiar with the term of curriculum. Curriculum is an essential tool for running the programme of educational instruction in the formal schooling. Each and every educational institution has some planned activities and programmes in the name of curriculum and co-curricular activites which are meaningful and significant for the students in their real life. Because through the various skillful and value-oriented curricular and co-curricular activities students can develop their physical, emotional and intellectual capacities that lead to their all round development. In order to have some clarity about its basic meaning, we have to know the origin of the term curriculum. The term curriculum is derived from Latin word Currere which means run . The very meaning of curriculum means a course to be run for reaching a certain goal or destination. Thus, in an educational institution, education is imagined as a race, with its aim as the goal and curriculum as the course leading to that goal. In a more precise term, we can define curriculum in the words of an educationist, Cunningham as a tool in the hands of artist (teacher) to mould his material (pupils) according to his ideals (aims and objectives) in his studio (school) This definition explains that curriculum is a course of study, designed to be followed at the various levels of education. In the opinion of Crow and Crow (as quoted in the book Safaya, R.N. and Shaida, B.D. (1996): Development of Educational Theory and Practice ) Curriculum includes all the learner s experiences in or outside the school that are included in a programme which has been devised to help his development, physically, emotionally, socially, spiritually and morally. Here the main logic of curriculum is to develop the total learning experiences of the students in their life. Principles and Theories of Education

key_points: 3 MEANING OF NATIONAL INTEGRATION We use the term Integration to mean the combination of different parts into a whole. But what is the actual meaning of National Integration National Integration is much more than a combination or unity among its members. It includes the feelings and sentiments of its citizens which govern their political and public behaviour. National Integration is the feeling of oneness where all its citizens are integrated through sharing with one another, their joys, sorrows, smiles, tears and a common interest in the welfare of the nation as a whole. The citizens of an integrated nation have mutual understanding, tolerance and respect for the culture, traditions and ways of life of the different sections of people of their country. They have common national ideals, common objectives, common interests and above all, a profound confidence in the future of the nation. This has necessitated mutually good and cordial relations amongst the countries of the world. And this is termed as International Understanding. key_points: 3 MEANING OF VALUE EDUCATION Before defining the meaning and concept of value education, let us discuss the meaning of value. Generally speaking, values are the norms of behaviour which have been evolved during the course of time in the social, moral and spiritual fields. It refers to the ideals in various acts of behaviour. In other words, value stands for the ideals of a man/woman that he/she lives for. Philosophically speaking, a human being is supposed to conduct himself and shape his/her life patterns by integrating his beliefs, ideas and attitudes. Values are those standards or code of moral behavior conditioned by one s cultural tenets and guided by his/her conscience. Thus, good of all qualities can be taken as the sole criterion for values. From psychological point of view, value is associated with the feeling aspect of behavior. It means that receiving knowledge about the value is not enough; it is necessary that it must be integrated into the personality of an individual so that it may be characterized.
